findings.title: self-heal-pipeline.md field-rules prose contradicts schema after 2026-05-24 fix — still names field 'version' but schema now uses 'schema_version'
plan.md canonical schema documents terminal status as 'closed' but all production audit files use 'fixed' — undocumented status value in every recent scan

plan.md schema missing closed status value used by all production audit files
rubric.json fingerprint test_case sha256_hex is a placeholder instruction string, not an actual hash
rubric.json categories dict does not include 'cosmetic', but scan files emit findings with category:'cosmetic'
ADR-005 in ifleet-integration-adrs.md references phantom file 'ifleet_elevation_plan.md'
README.md splittasks link is a placeholder (https://github.com/...)
lane-scheduler-spec.md has hard-coded /Users/Seb absolute paths in two places
self-heal-pipeline.md synthetic proof path uses absolute /Users/Seb reference
20260604T050000Z.json uses scan_id field instead of audit_id, file string instead of file_globs array, and is missing fingerprint fields
findings.detail: The 2026-06-04 scan file used scan_id instead of the canonical audit_id field name, stored file paths as a bare string 'file' instead of the file_globs array, and omitted the fingerprint field from all 6 findings. These deviations break any tooling that reads the canonical schema (e.g. regression detection, audit-triager).
findings.fix_sketch: Rename scan_id → audit_id. Change each finding's file string to file_globs array. Compute and add fingerprint for each finding using rubric sha256-v1 algorithm.

findings.title: index.json closing_pr field uses string values ("direct-fix", branch names) instead of integer PR number per canonical schema
findings.detail: self-heal-pipeline.md canonical schema specifies closing_pr as an integer PR number (or null/0 for direct fixes). index.json entries from 2026-05-21 through 2026-06-04 use the strings 'direct-fix' and 'audit/nightly-YYYY-MM-DD', which fail type checks and break any tooling that expects an integer.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace all closing_pr string values with 0 (direct fix, no PR opened). Future entries that close via a real PR should use the integer PR number.

findings.title: Proposer ranking bug: IMPORTANT regression scores 110 which exceeds CRITICAL non-regression base of 100
findings.detail: proposer-spec.md §3 scoring table: IMPORTANT base=80, regression bonus=+30 → effective score=110. CRITICAL non-regression base=100. An IMPORTANT regression outranks a CRITICAL non-regression, which is counterintuitive — CRITICAL always means 'active threat or guaranteed failure' which should dominate IMPORTANT at any regression status.
findings.fix_sketch: Cap the regression bonus per severity class: IMPORTANT regression ≤ 99 (CRITICAL base − 1), COSMETIC regression ≤ 49 (IMPORTANT base − 1). Only CRITICAL findings may score ≥ 100.

findings.title: proposer-spec.md audit-triager cannot retrieve detail and fix_sketch from index.json which only carries summary fields
findings.detail: index.json carries only summary fields (id, severity, category, title, status, file_globs). The audit-triager needs detail and fix_sketch to generate actionable lane briefs. The proposer-spec.md §2 does not document that the proposer/triager must load the originating scan file to get these fields.
findings.fix_sketch: Document in the §2 audit findings row that the Proposer must load the originating scan file (<repo>/.audits/<audit_id>.json) to retrieve detail and fix_sketch when surfacing a finding.

findings.title: proposer-spec.md closed.json suppression in section 2 is not distinguished from section 3 status pre-filter creating confusion about their separate purposes
findings.detail: §2 lists closed.json as 'Suppress already-resolved findings'. §3 pre-filter drops any finding with status not in ['open','regression'], which already handles findings closed in index.json. A reader cannot tell why closed.json exists separately or what work it does that the pre-filter doesn't.
findings.fix_sketch: Clarify in the §2 closed.json row: it covers resolutions that predate index.json establishment, and provides fingerprint history for cross-session regression detection. These are distinct from the §3 status pre-filter which only acts on index.json status fields.

findings.title: proposer-spec.md lane-budget filter has no explicit else branch for the 3-4 lane or 2-4h middle range case
findings.detail: §3 step 3 documents two cases: ≥5 lanes ≥4h → cap 3, and ≤2 lanes ≤2h → allow 6. The 3-4 lane case and the 2-4h middle duration case are not covered. Implementors would be left to guess whether the default cap applies or something in between.
findings.fix_sketch: Add explicit else branch: 3-4 lanes or 2-4h range or mixed signals → cap at 5 lanes (default). This makes the filter complete and removes implementation ambiguity.

findings.title: proposer-spec.md IMPORTANT roadmap-affecting score assumes milestones have owned glob sets which ROADMAP.md does not define
findings.detail: §3 scoring: 'IMPORTANT findings affecting roadmap items: 80. Affected = the finding's globs overlap a roadmap item's owned glob set.' ROADMAP.md milestones have no 'owned glob set' field. An implementor following this spec would have no way to determine which findings 'affect' which milestone.
findings.fix_sketch: Document that glob-set ownership must be inferred from milestone descriptions (e.g. if a milestone title mentions a file or pattern), or as a conservative default treat all IMPORTANT findings as roadmap-adjacent (scoring 80). Note this is an open design decision.

findings.title: proposer-spec.md roadmap unblocked score assumes predecessors can be identified as done but ROADMAP.md uses no completed status
findings.detail: §3: 'Roadmap items unblocked = all predecessor IDs in ROADMAP.md marked done.' ROADMAP.md uses status values planned, deferred, in-progress — none of which is 'done' or 'completed'. As of 2026-06-07 no milestone uses a terminal status, making this scoring row permanently inactive without documentation.
findings.fix_sketch: Document that 'done' maps to ROADMAP.md status:completed (the terminal value). Note that as of 2026-06-07 no milestone is completed so this scoring class is inactive. When milestones begin completing, update ROADMAP.md to use status:completed.

findings.title: proposer-spec.md D6 references rejections.jsonl for the minus-40 penalty but section 2 input table references last-proposal.json creating two conflicting sources
findings.detail: §2 input: 'Yesterday's proposal: ~/.omc/proposer/state/last-proposal.json — track Sebastian's accept/reject pattern'. D6: 'store reject reasons in rejections.jsonl and feed into next-night's −40 penalty calculation'. These appear to be two conflicting sources of truth for the penalty. An implementor would not know which file to read for penalty calculation.
findings.fix_sketch: Clarify the two-file protocol: last-proposal.json is the mutable daily state file updated at accept/reject time. rejections.jsonl is an append-only audit log of reject events derived from last-proposal.json. The −40 penalty reads from rejections.jsonl. Both are needed; they are complementary, not conflicting.

findings.title: plan.md findings schema detail field documents 2-3 paragraph description but a single JSON string cannot contain formatted paragraphs
findings.detail: plan.md Phase 1 schema example shows: 'detail': '2-3 paragraph description'. A JSON string field cannot contain paragraph-formatted text in a useful way. All production scan files use 2-3 sentence descriptions in practice. The comment misrepresents the expected format and could cause an implementor to write verbosely structured detail fields.
findings.fix_sketch: Change '2-3 paragraph description' to '2-3 sentence description' in the schema comment to match actual production usage.

findings.title: index.json 2026-05-22 batch contains 9 fabricated sequential byte-rotation fingerprints that do not match rubric sha256-v1 algorithm
findings.detail: 9 entries from the 2026-05-22 audit batch have fingerprints following a clear sequential byte-rotation pattern (a1b2c3d4..., b2c3d4e5..., c3d4e5f6..., etc.). These are fabricated placeholders, not sha256 hashes of the category|globs|title concatenation. Regression detection would fail to match these findings against future scans of the same bugs.
findings.fix_sketch: Compute correct sha256-v1 fingerprints for all 9 entries using rubric normalization: lowercase(category)|sorted_globs_comma_joined|lowercase_strip_punct_whitespace_collapse(title). Replace fabricated values.

findings.title: index.json 2026-05-27 batch contains 3 fingerprints truncated to 62-63 hex characters instead of the required 64 for sha256
findings.detail: 3 entries from the 2026-05-27 batch (9f3c1d2e, b7d4e1a3, c2f5b8e7) have fingerprints of length 63, 62, and 62 hex characters respectively. SHA-256 always produces 64 hex characters. These are also clearly fabricated (sequential pattern) but truncated, making them doubly invalid.
findings.fix_sketch: Compute correct 64-character sha256-v1 fingerprints for all 3 entries using the rubric algorithm. Replace truncated values.

findings.title: index.json is described as open findings rollup in plan.md but contains all findings including closed and fixed status entries
findings.detail: plan.md Phase 1 schema doc says the scanner 'Updates <repo-root>/.audits/index.json (open findings rollup)'. But index.json in practice contains all historical findings across all statuses (open, fixed, closed). The open_findings count field tracks open subset correctly but the file description is misleading.
findings.fix_sketch: Update plan.md description to 'full findings ledger — all statuses; open_findings field tracks the open subset'. This is accurate and prevents implementors from assuming the file should be pruned to only open findings.

findings.title: nightly_audits filenames mix ISO 8601 format and compact format creating inconsistency
findings.detail: index.json nightly_audits array contains filenames in two formats: ISO 8601 with separators (2026-05-21T17:20:59Z.json) and compact without separators (20260527T041500Z.json). This is cosmetic but hinders sorting by filename and creates confusion about the canonical naming convention.
findings.fix_sketch: Adopt one format going forward. Recommendation: compact format (20260607T041244Z.json) to match the pattern used in the IFleet and factory audit branches. Document in plan.md that new scan files use compact ISO format YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ.

findings.title: index.json fixed_this_run is a transient session count that does not belong in a persistent ledger file
findings.detail: index.json contained a fixed_this_run: 6 field from the 2026-06-04 session. This is a session-scoped count that becomes stale and misleading the moment the next audit runs. The persistent ledger should only contain durable state; transient session metrics belong in the per-scan file or only in memory.
findings.fix_sketch: Remove fixed_this_run from index.json. Per-session fix counts are available from the scan file's findings_count and status fields.

findings.title: plan.md schema comment says 2-3 paragraph description rather than 2-3 sentence description misleading about appropriate detail length
findings.detail: plan.md schema example field detail shows '2-3 paragraph description' as the placeholder value comment. A JSON string field containing 2-3 full paragraphs would be unwieldy for the audit-triager to surface in a Discord message. All production scan files use 2-3 sentence summaries. The wording is cosmetically misleading about expected detail verbosity.
findings.fix_sketch: Update schema comment from '2-3 paragraph description' to '2-3 sentence description'.
